[MUQATIL:27:36-37/r1] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The envoys asked for water neither from rain nor a spring; Sulayman ran horses until they sweated, strained the sweat into crystal cups, and impressed them. Gabriel told him the box’s contents; Sulayman disclosed them and returned the gift.
[MUQATIL:27:36-37/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Sulayman asks whether they would support him with wealth and says God’s gifts of Islam, prophethood, and troops are better than theirs.
[MUQATIL:27:36-37/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | People rejoice when they exchange gifts, but Sulayman does not rejoice in this gift; he wants them to accept Islam.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A subjunctive after أو is governed by an understood أن, as after fa and wāw; أن is not normally stated aloud.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الحصين بن حمام المري | reports | The poem ولولا رجال ... أو أسوءك shows an understood أن because the verb cannot be coordinated directly with لولا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · عمرو بن معدي كرب | reports | The line تحية بينهم ضرب وجيع supports the idiom comparing a state or greeting with an action, which Sībawayh uses to explain the Medinan reading. | mentions 42:51
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · الخليل | holds | For the Aʿshā's إن تركبوا ... أو تنزلون, al-Khalīl parses the clauses as alternatives: one would be the case or the other, as if أتركبون were used.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · يونس | prefers | Yūnus raises أو تنزلون as a fresh clause, understood as أو أنتم نازلون; Sībawayh says this analysis is easier and applies it to أو يرسل in the verse. | mentions 42:51
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · زهير | reports | Al-Khalīl compares the strained coordination analysis with Zuhayr's ولا سابق شيئا إذا كان جائيا, where coordination is only imagined from the sense.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Sībawayh says the coordination analysis is remote because if it were ordinary coordination it would also work after fa and wāw; the semantic relation can instead prompt a new clause, as in لا تأته فيشتمك.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The subjunctive after أو can mean إلا أن; Imruʾ al-Qays's أو نموت فنعذرا means unless we die, parallel to لألزمنك أو تقضيني.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Rafʿ after أو is grammatical either by coordinating the following clause with the first or by starting a new clause.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · ذوا الرمة | reports | Dhū al-Rumma's verse allows either coordination with لا تنفك or a new clause at أو نرمي بها.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In commands such as الزمه أو يتقيك, the subjunctive means unless he protects you; raising is a fresh clause because the clauses cannot be coordinated.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · زياد الأعجم | reports | Ziyād al-Aʿjam's verse وكنت إذا غمزت قناة قوم كسرت كعوبها أو تستقيما illustrates subjunctive with the sense إلا أن; rafʿ would instead start a clause.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابأو)#478/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · طرفة بن العبد | reports | Ṭarafa's أو أنا مفتدي exemplifies a raised independent clause after هو قاتلي أو أفتدي منه.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Rāʾ behaves as if doubled, so it prevents imāla in راشد and فراش and strengthens fatḥ of nearby alifs.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | They often open حمار قاسم for qāf, though imāla is more common than in مال قاسم because the intervening pattern has two kasras; جارم قاسم does not behave identically.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Speakers who say حمار قاسم also say سفار قبل because rāʾ can change in construct phrases or as the ending of a masculine name.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In فار قبل and كافر قبل, a single silent consonant intervenes and the following rāʾ is kasra, making imāla required for these speakers; a speaker who says جاد does not say فار.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Imāla in دنانير is more expected because rāʾ is farther from the alif; genitive behavior matches كافر, and some speakers also say مناشيط.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | At pause, forms such as داع do not imale because the kasra is not pronounced; in حمار, the doubled rāʾ similarly governs the preceding alif.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Some imale the hāʾ and preceding vowel in مهارى; Arab forms ضربة and أخذه liken hāʾ to alif, so the preceding sound is imaled.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The rāʾ is weaker than qāf in these contexts: speakers who say أراد أن يضربها قاسم also say راشد, and those who say بمال قاسم also say بمال راشد.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Forms عفرا, عيرا, and عمران can be compared with علقا, ضيقا, and حمقان; some imale عفرا because initial kasra precedes a final alif, treating it like حبلى.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Imāla in عفرا is especially plausible by analogy with عرقا and forms of يعقرها; if kasra can incline the alif, yā is an even stronger trigger.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When rāʾ follows an alif, the alif is not imaled in nominative or accusative forms like حمار; in genitive it is imaled because rāʾ acts like two kasra consonants.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | They imale النغران because initial kasra precedes an alif after a root consonant, which they liken to an alif built into a word such as حبلى.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | They say عمران with imāla but not برقان or حمقان because those forms contain emphatic consonants.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some who imale عمران also imale عقران, since the emphatic is distant; in فراش and جراب fatḥ is preferred because their alif is added, not like feminine حبلى.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A kasra on rāʾ after alif can overcome an earlier emphatic, allowing imāla in قارب, غارم, and طارد.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Forms such as فارق and مفاريق take fatḥ like ناعق, منافق, and مناشيط because an emphatic follows the alif.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some Arabs imale الكافرون, الكافرين, الكافر, and المنابر when a consonant separates rāʾ from alif; rāʾ is distant and close in articulation to yā.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Another group opens these alifs in nominative and accusative but imales them in genitive, treating case as the condition for imāla.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض من يقول مررت بالحمار | reports | Some who say مررت بالحمار still pronounce مررت بالكافر with fatḥ, since their usual form عابد has an open alif and the ending varies.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Imāla in كافر is more common than in قادر because qāf is emphatic; some Arabs with sound Arabic nevertheless imale قادر when rāʾ is kasra.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالراء)#720/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · هدبة بن خشرم | reports | Hudbah ibn Khashram's verse uses قادر with imāla, witnessing the reported variant مررت بقادر before kasra on rāʾ.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A verb raised between two jussives may explain or substitute for the first result when both express the same action.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | When conjunctions such as ثم, ف, و, or أو link a second verb between the conditional jussives, that verb is also jussive.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | These conjunctions share the second verb in the grammatical government imposed on the first.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Raising is impossible under this coordination; تعشو was raised because it occupies the place of a circumstantial عاشيا, unlike a coordinated verb.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | Al-Khalil allows accusative after ف or و by construing an implied أن and a nominal phrase, but says jussive is the proper construction.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | Jussive is preferred because the intended meaning is already jussive, and the nearest governing construction should apply without crossing into another syntactic domain.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The accusative in Ibn Zuhayr's line is good because فيثبتها means the person slips unless he plants his foot.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After إن تأتني فأحدثك, the final verb can only be raised: the conditional sequence has ended, so the following clause is detached rather than coordinated within it.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With إن تأتني آتك فأحدثك, raising can start an independent clause, while accusative after ف or و is also possible as in the interposed-verb pattern.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r18] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | ثم does not license accusative through an implied أن as ف and و can; its meaning differs from و, and it coordinates rather than starting a new clause mid-condition.

YH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r19] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Between the conditional clauses ثم requires jussive, but after the whole conditional ends either jussive or raising is possible.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Zuhayr's raised يغنها is also possible as an independent clause, paraphrased as the man who keeps relying on others does not enrich himself.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r20] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Quranic examples show jussive after ثم in a completed conditional, including the fighting and turning-away clauses. | mentions 3:111, 47:38
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r21] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعضهم | reports | Some reportedly read يغفر and يعذب in the accusative after the conjunctions in 2:284. | mentions 2:284
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r22] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | Raising after ف is the standard choice when the preceding conditional answer is a nominal clause, because the following clause behaves as it would outside a condition.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r23] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In the charity verse, نكفر is raised after فهو خير لكم because it follows an independent nominal clause. | mentions 2:271
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r24] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض القراء | reports | Some readers raised ويذرهم by attaching it to the syntactic position of the preceding clause as a conditional answer. | mentions 7:186
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r25] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Accusative can match jussive when the whole preceding clause occupies an accusative syntactic position, as in the cited verse of poetry.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r26] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | After a conditional response containing لن or لم, a following verb is raised when it is not governed by that negative particle.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r27] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | prefers | Match the response tense to the conditional: present condition with لا آتك and past condition with لم آتك; mismatched tense and negation are poor.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r28] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Accusative after ف or و in a conditional sequence is weak and not the normal form, though somewhat more acceptable because the result depends on the first act.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r29] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Poetry by al-A'sha supplies an accusative example; the construction remains nonstandard, and its sense resembles a promise qualified by إن شاء الله.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In al-Hutay'a's conditional, تعشو is raised as a circumstantial description, equivalent to arriving while blind.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Al-Khalil treats تلمم as an appositional substitute for the first verb, specifying that coming means visiting, like explanatory apposition between nouns.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | In a verse attributed through al-Asma'i from Abu Amr, يغدوا substitutes for لا يحفلوا, and arriving groomed explains their lack of concern.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | إن تأتنا تسألنا نعطك is allowed only as a slip followed by self-correction, since asking is not the same as coming; a comparable noun slip is مررت برجل حمار.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Al-Khalil reads يضاعف as like the preceding result because increased punishment is the encounter with sin. | mentions 25:68, 25:69
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The same explanatory substitution works when إحسان is specified by doing good, giving, or carrying the person.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايرتفعبينالجزمينوينجزمبينهما)#488/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | إن تأتني آتك أقل ذاك is normally invalid because speaking is not coming, except as a tolerated slip like تسألنا.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The seven emphatic consonants block imāla when adjacent before alif: both raise the tongue toward the upper palate, so the emphatic articulation prevails.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | Some imale مال in the genitive by analogy with مالك when the following kāf is a proper name; other speakers imale it in every case to show its original kasra.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعضهم | reports | Some speakers use fatḥ in مال قاسم, مال ملق, and مال ينقل, especially before connected emphatics; one group distinguishes a separated following word from a connected one.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r12] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Imāla persists in stable forms such as عماد and عابد before a separate قاسم because their endings do not vary by case, unlike مال.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r13] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | They do not imale in لم يضربها الذي تعلم because the alif has disappeared; it is unlike the enduring alif in حبلى or مرمى.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r14] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | They open أراد أن يضبطا before emphatic ṭāʾ, but imale يعقلا because qāf is kasra; some analogically imale عرقا and ضيقا, though Sībawayh calls such forms rare.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r15] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Particles حتى, أما, إلا, لا, and ما generally resist imāla, unlike nouns; al-Khalīl allows it if a particle is used as a personal name, and أنى is imaled as a noun-like adverb.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r16] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Letter names با and تا are imaled as nouns for spoken letters, and يا in يا زيد is imaled because of its yā.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r17] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Even speakers who imale مال do not generally imale hollow forms such as ساق, قار, or غاب; the medial weak alif is stronger and the imāla is less accepted.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r2] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The same emphatics generally block imāla when they follow alif or are separated from it by one or two letters.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r3] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | He compares the sound substitution صقت for صبقت: before qāf, speakers replace the nearer sibilant with a sound closer to qāf in articulation.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r4] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | An emphatic one letter before alif does not block imāla when that letter is preceded by kasra; lowering the tongue is easier than raising it.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r5] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | With an initial kasra and two intervening letters, a silent emphatic can allow imāla because the earlier kasra makes the alif behave as if the emphatic were kasra.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r6] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · بعض من يقول قفاف | reports | Some speakers who imale قفاف still use fatḥ in مصباح: the silent emphatic is followed by fatḥa, making it act like an emphatic followed by alif; both patterns are Arabic.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r7] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | He records imāla in قزحا and ضمنا, and in عرقا and ملغا, by analogy with patterns such as صفاف, قفاف, غانم, and قائم.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r8] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | Alifs in ناب, مال, and باع remain subject to imāla because they stand where yā would; خاف, feminine حبلى, and غزا have comparable underlying causes.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايمتنعمنالإمالةمنالألفاتالتيأملتهافيمامضى)#719/r9] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | The alif in geminate فاعل and in مفاعل is not normally imaled: the consonant before it is open and no kasra follows it.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجزاءينجزمفيهالفعل)#489/r1] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A response is jussive when it answers a command, prohibition, question, wish, or offer, because it depends on that first expression.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجزاءينجزمفيهالفعل)#489/r10] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | holds | A jussive after prohibition is apt when avoiding the act causes the result; it is poor if the result is not caused by avoidance, while an independent raised clause or ف is fine.
[SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمنالجزاءينجزمفيهالفعل)#489/r11] SIBAWAYH, d. 180 · author | reports | A trusted Arab's لا تذهب به تغلب عليه confirms the jussive pattern where the prohibited action would allow the consequence.
